scenarios.name: System Information Discovery
scenarios.description: Emulates system information discovery to generate realistic reconnaissance telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Executes a set of system information commands to collect details about the operating system, hardware, kernel and installed packages, saving results to a log file for telemetry analysis. Designed to be safe and non-destructive; artefacts are cleaned up by default.

scenarios.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
scenarios.description: Collects network configuration details to simulate host-level network reconnaissance.
scenarios.fullDescription: Runs a series of network configuration commands (for example ip addr, ip route, ifconfig, netstat) to collect interface, routing and port information and writes results to a log file. All generated files are removed during standard cleanup unless instructed otherwise.

scenarios.name: DNS reconnaissance or enumeration via DNSRecon
scenarios.description: Creates and executes a benign DNS reconnaissance script to simulate domain and subdomain enumeration.
scenarios.fullDescription: Writes a small Python DNS reconnaissance script to a temporary directory which performs DNS lookups against common subdomains of a target domain, logs results and then cleans up. The implementation is non-aggressive and intended only to generate detectable DNS query patterns for analytics testing.
scenarios.command: run "DNS reconnaissance or enumeration via DNSRecon"
scenarios.fullCommand: signalbench run "DNS reconnaissance or enumeration via DNSRecon"

scenarios.name: Network Service Discovery
scenarios.description: Simulates scanning for network services to identify open ports and running services.
scenarios.fullDescription: Performs safe port checks on localhost targets and produces a scan results file. For non-local targets a simulated result is generated to avoid unintended network scanning while still producing realistic telemetry.

scenarios.name: System Network Connections Discovery
scenarios.description: Collects active network connection and listening port information to map local network activity.
scenarios.fullDescription: Executes tools such as ss, netstat and lsof to enumerate current network connections and associated processes, writes a connections log file and cleans up by default. Useful for generating process-to-network telemetry.

scenarios.name: Memory Dumping
scenarios.description: Simulates memory dumping activity to produce telemetry associated with credential harvesting attempts.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates a simulated memory dump file and associated analysis logs to mimic the process of extracting credentials from process memory. The simulation writes synthetic content and is non-destructive. Generated artefacts are removed during cleanup unless preserved with flags.

scenarios.name: Keylogging
scenarios.description: Simulates keystroke capture to generate telemetry that detection tools can exercise.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates a benign keylogger-like output file containing synthetic keystroke records for a configured duration. The simulation does not capture real user input and writes only test data for analysis; artefacts are cleaned up by default.

scenarios.name: Credentials in Files
scenarios.description: Searches for and creates test credential files to emulate harvesting from configuration files.
scenarios.fullDescription: Generates sample credential-containing files (such as .env and config.json) in controllable locations and runs a search routine to demonstrate credential discovery telemetry. All created files are removed during cleanup unless preservation is requested.

scenarios.name: OS Credential Dumping: Proc Filesystem
scenarios.description: Simulates analysis of the /proc filesystem to generate telemetry like proc-based memory inspection.
scenarios.fullDescription: Enumerates processes under /proc, inspects maps entries and creates synthetic memory segment files using safe utilities to produce realistic telemetry patterns associated with proc-based credential inspection. The simulation logs findings to a session directory and cleans up by default.

scenarios.name: Hydra Brute Force Tool Simulation
scenarios.description: Simulates execution of a brute-force tool by downloading a benign test file and attempting execution to generate detection telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Downloads a harmless test binary and saves it under a name such as 'hydra' to emulate the presence and attempted execution of a brute-force tool. The operation is intended to create file and process telemetry while remaining non-destructive; files are cleaned up by default.

scenarios.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
scenarios.description: Generates obfuscated artefacts and demonstrates deobfuscation to exercise static-analysis and detection logic.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates files using a variety of obfuscation methods (base64, XOR, packing, string concatenation) and optionally executes deobfuscated content to produce end-to-end telemetry. All artefacts are removed during standard cleanup unless retention is requested.

scenarios.name: Process Injection
scenarios.description: Implements controlled, harmless process-injection simulations to generate relevant telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Supports a range of injection-like techniques (ptrace-based, LD_PRELOAD and shared-library approaches) by compiling local test code and performing safe operations that produce observable process and memory access telemetry. The implementation is controlled and reversible; compilation artefacts are cleaned up by default.

scenarios.name: Disable Linux Audit Logs
scenarios.description: Creates benign artefacts that mimic actions to disable audit logging, without changing live audit configuration.
scenarios.fullDescription: Writes a simulated audit rules file and demonstrates the commands that would disable audit logging in a real attack; it does not apply changes to system audit configuration. Files produced are removed during standard cleanup.

scenarios.name: Clear Command History
scenarios.description: Simulates clearing shell history to generate telemetry associated with anti-forensic activity.
scenarios.fullDescription: Backs up the current shell history and replaces it with a benign placeholder to simulate clearing activity; restores the original history during cleanup to avoid permanent user impact. All actions are logged for analysis.

scenarios.name: Path Interception
scenarios.description: Simulates modification of environment variables to demonstrate PATH or LD_LIBRARY_PATH interception telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Documents current PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH, creates a test directory with benign executables placed at the front of PATH and records the resultant execution behaviour. All modifications are reversible and removed during cleanup.

scenarios.name: Masquerading (crond)
scenarios.description: Simulates process masquerading by creating a copy of a system binary with a legitimate daemon name in a non-standard location.
scenarios.fullDescription: Copies a system binary to a temporary location with a name such as 'crond' and optionally executes it to produce process creation telemetry consistent with masquerading detections. The simulation avoids altering system binaries and cleans up all created files.

scenarios.name: Advanced Command and Scripting Interpreter
scenarios.description: Executes commands and scripts with a variety of obfuscation methods to exercise detection capabilities for interpreters.
scenarios.fullDescription: Supports multiple interpreter types (bash, python, perl) and obfuscation techniques (base64, hex, variable concatenation, IFS manipulation). Creates temporary scripts, executes them to generate telemetry and removes artefacts during cleanup.
scenarios.fullCommand: signalbench run "Advanced Command and Scripting Interpreter"

scenarios.name: Possible C2 via dnscat2
scenarios.description: Demonstrates command-and-control-like behaviour by downloading and executing a benign test file named to emulate dnscat2.
scenarios.fullDescription: Downloads a harmless test file representative of known C2 tooling and executes it with innocuous parameters to generate DNS-based C2 telemetry. The operation is intended to produce observable network and process traces while remaining non-destructive; generated files are removed during cleanup.

scenarios.name: Uncommon Remote Shell Commands
scenarios.description: Generates telemetry for execution of uncommon command names to trigger baseline anomaly detection.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates several uniquely named benign executables (prefixed to indicate test provenance), executes them briefly to produce process creation telemetry and then removes them. Names are synthetic and chosen to exercise detection rules that flag novel or suspicious command names.

scenarios.name: Python Script Execution
scenarios.description: Creates and runs a Python script with scripted behaviours to generate interpreter telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Writes a Python script that performs benign reconnaissance or file operations, executes it and logs outputs. The script is synthetic and cleaned up on completion unless retention is requested for analysis.

scenarios.name: SSH Lateral Movement
scenarios.description: Simulates lateral movement attempts using SSH to exercise network and authentication telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Attempts SSH connections to configured targets using key-based authentication where possible, records connection attempts and outcomes in logs, and cleans up any temporary artefacts. Designed to generate SSH client and connection telemetry for detection tuning.

scenarios.name: Startup Folder (Linux autostart .desktop)
scenarios.description: Generates autostart persistence telemetry by creating a .desktop entry in the user's autostart directory.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates a properly formatted .desktop file in ~/.config/autostart that will execute a benign command at user login. The implementation respects desktop standards, creates observable file system and autorun telemetry and removes the entry during standard cleanup.

scenarios.name: Cron Job
scenarios.description: Creates a scheduled cron job entry to simulate scheduled persistence behaviour.
scenarios.fullDescription: Modifies the current user's crontab to add a harmless scheduled entry that executes a benign command, producing observable crontab modification telemetry. The original crontab is restored during cleanup unless preservation is requested.

scenarios.name: Create or Modify System Process
scenarios.description: Creates or modifies service definitions to produce telemetry associated with service-based persistence.
scenarios.fullDescription: Writes service unit or init scripts (systemd units, init.d scripts or rc.local entries) in a controlled manner and simulates installation where privilege permits. All created files are removed during cleanup unless explicitly preserved.

scenarios.name: Web Shell Deployment
scenarios.description: Deploys benign web shell files in a web document root to generate web-application persistence telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates harmless web shell files (PHP, JSP or similar) in a specified web root to emulate attacker-deployed web shells for detection testing. Files are created only in provided, permitted directories and removed during cleanup.

scenarios.name: Sudoers Modification
scenarios.description: Simulates creation of sudoers entries to demonstrate telemetry for privilege elevation via sudo configuration changes.
scenarios.fullDescription: Writes a temporary sudoers file in /etc/sudoers.d/ (simulation mode by default) and validates syntax; the tool does not modify live sudoers by default unless run with explicit elevated privileges and consent. Artefacts are removed during cleanup.

scenarios.name: Sudo Unsigned Integer Privilege Escalation (CVE test)
scenarios.description: Demonstrates the sudo negative/unsigned integer invocation pattern to generate detection telemetry for CVE-2019-14287-like activity.
scenarios.fullDescription: Attempts to run harmless commands using the -u#-1 and -u#4294967295 invocation patterns in a controlled manner to produce logs representative of an attempt to exploit sudo integer handling vulnerabilities. The operation is non-destructive and intended solely for telemetry generation.

scenarios.name: SUID Binary
scenarios.description: Creates a harmless binary and sets the SUID bit to generate file-permission change telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates a small test executable, sets the SUID bit and demonstrates the permission change and its implications for detection. The file is removed during cleanup to avoid persistent changes to the system.

scenarios.name: Local Account Creation
scenarios.description: Simulates creation of local user accounts to generate account-management telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates harmless test files representing new user account entries and logs the simulated account creation activity; by default it avoids modifying system account files and cleans up all artefacts.

scenarios.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation (Simulation)
scenarios.description: Simulates common local privilege escalation exploit activity to generate telemetry without performing real exploitation.
scenarios.fullDescription: Produces realistic logs and artefact patterns associated with known local privilege-escalation exploits (for example Dirty Pipe or Dirty COW) while never executing destructive or unauthorised exploit code. The simulation adapts output to the detected kernel version for realism and cleans up generated files.

scenarios.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
scenarios.description: Simulates data exfiltration over protocols such as DNS, ICMP or HTTP to generate network exfiltration telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Encodes synthetic data for the selected protocol and simulates or performs controlled transfers to generate detectable patterns. All data used is synthetic and transfers are performed only to authorised test endpoints or simulated locally; artefacts are removed during cleanup.

scenarios.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
scenarios.description: Establishes command-and-control-like communication using non-application layer protocols to generate network telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Implements controlled C2-style communication over protocols such as ICMP, TCP or UDP using safe utilities to produce beaconing and payload-exchange telemetry. Communications are conducted only with authorised test endpoints and are non-destructive; logs and temporary files are removed during cleanup.

scenarios.name: Traffic Signalling
scenarios.description: Uses scheduled tasks to install network filters for covert signalling telemetry.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates cron entries that install and remove simple traffic filters (iptables or tc) on a schedule to emulate covert signalling mechanisms. All operations are reversible and logged; created cron tasks and filter scripts are removed during cleanup.

scenarios.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
scenarios.description: Downloads benign test files from external sources and attempts execution to generate telemetry for tool transfer detection.
scenarios.fullDescription: Performs controlled downloads using curl or wget from configured test URLs, makes files executable and attempts safe execution to create file, process and network telemetry. All artefacts are removed during cleanup unless retention is explicitly requested.

scenarios.name: Suspicious GitHub Tool Transfer
scenarios.description: Generates telemetry by performing HTTP requests to synthetic GitHub paths to emulate tool-download behaviour.
scenarios.fullDescription: Creates curl requests to a set of synthetic GitHub repository URLs (predictable prefix) which typically return non-200 responses; this produces observable HTTP request telemetry without downloading real malicious content. All request logs are stored and cleaned up during standard cleanup.

scenarios.name: PACEMAKER (benign simulation)
scenarios.description: Deploys a benign simulation of PACEMAKER-like behaviour to generate /proc-focused credential-harvesting telemetry without using proprietary signatures.
scenarios.fullDescription: Extracts and runs a harmless simulation binary that emulates documented behaviour of certain proc-filesystem credential inspection techniques to produce realistic telemetry for analytics research. The simulation includes launcher scripts and creates synthetic credential artefacts in temporary directories. The simulation does not attempt to reproduce exact file hashes or external signature sets and avoids referencing third-party YARA rule repositories.
